Whitepaper — AI-Assisted Enterprise Asset Management

Engineering AI-driven data, agent, and UI layers for enterprise asset management.

The client had an existing asset management platform, but adoption stalled because Asset Managers still carried too much manual work. Intelligaia engineered the data, automation, RAG, agent, and UI layers needed to move from manual reconciliation to evidence-backed, AI-assisted operations.

Client stateExisting product · low adoption · Asset Manager-heavy workflows
Core challengeFragmented data · manual reconciliation · informal coverage rules
What we builtData, automation, RAG, agents, workflow APIs, dynamic UI
DirectionGuided operations · zero, low, and high touch
01 · Project context

The product existed. The operational burden still remained.

The client already had an asset management platform and a defined delivery process. The challenge was that the product was not yet reducing enough of the manual work required to run the operation at scale. Asset Managers were still validating orders, comparing inventory files, reconciling contracts, applying customer-specific rules, and preparing review packages by hand.

When Intelligaia started, we knew some of this work could be converted into deterministic automation, and other parts required AI-assisted reasoning. The real engineering job was to identify the boundary between the two.

"Some work was repetitive and rules-driven. Other work depended on judgment, historical context, and customer-specific rules. That separation became the foundation for the AI and automation roadmap." — CTO, Intelligaia

03 · What Intelligaia proposed

Two operational shifts. One clean line between automation and AI.

Both areas were heavily manual and required Asset Managers to consolidate information across multiple systems. Both also had enough repeated logic to be automated, and enough ambiguity to benefit from AI assistance.

01

Automate asset reconciliation.

A reconciliation engine that classifies assets and surfaces exceptions — replacing manual file-by-file consolidation across inventory, contract, and coverage data.

02

Operationalize coverage policies.

Customer-specific service coverage strategy converted from Asset Manager knowledge into executable rules that drive onboarding, discovery, and lifecycle recommendations.

04 · Automation vs AI

Repeatable process automation. Operational reasoning. Drawn apart on purpose.

This classification made the roadmap credible. Not every problem needed AI, and not every problem could be solved through deterministic rules. The team made the line explicit, then layered three touch models on top.

Category
Why this approach
Scope examples
Automation
Used when the process was rules-driven, structured, and repeatable.
Order processing, purchase-program mapping, engagement creation, task routing, scheduled refreshes, contract linkage, basic validations.
AI assistance
Used when the decision required context, ranking, interpretation, prediction, or explanation.
Asset Manager recommendation, overload prediction, new vs. renew suggestion, asset scope reasoning, coverage policy suggestion, anomaly explanation, customer summaries.
Human approval
Used when decisions affected customer commitments, contracts, coverage, or financial workflow.
Final Asset Manager assignment, customer scope sign-off, coverage policy edits, lifecycle approval, service strategy, customer-facing package approval.

Three touch models — how far automation and AI can safely go

Zero touch

Fully automated where confidence is high.

The system processes data, applies rules, generates outputs, and publishes them without Asset Manager review.

Low touch

Automation with selective review.

The system performs the analysis and prepares recommendations. Selected exceptions reach a Asset Manager.

High touch

Human-led with AI assistance.

Asset Managers review and approve all meaningful customer, contract, or coverage decisions.

05 · The clearest example

Asset reconciliation — automation and AI working together.

The existing process required Asset Managers to manually consolidate evidence from multiple tools. Intelligaia built a structured reconciliation engine where deterministic checks happen first, AI supports reasoning when the evidence is incomplete or conflicting, and the Asset Manager approves with full context.

06 · AI implementation

A governed RAG and agent system — not a generic chatbot.

The goal was never to let a model freely answer questions from raw data. The goal was a controlled operational AI layer that retrieves the right context, calls approved tools, reasons over evidence, and acts through the UI.

RAG and agent architecture

→

→

→

→

RAG layer

Context retrieval

Process rules, coverage policies, customer context, and historical decisions — indexed by workflow stage and persona.

Agent layer

Specialized operational agents

Onboarding, assignment, reconciliation, policy execution, discovery, and narrative — each with one defined role.

Tool layer

Controlled enterprise actions

Governed APIs with input and output schemas, permissions, and approval boundaries.

08 · Built workflows

Four workflows where guided operations replaced manual consolidation.

Each workflow ships with a structured UI component populated by the agent and tool layer — so the Asset Manager sees evidence, confidence, and the next action in one place.

Each card shows a close-up of the central work area of one workflow surface — chrome, navigation, and branding are intentionally cropped out so the focus is on the interaction pattern itself.
Workflow 01

AI interface to review the asset registry

Asset Managers review asset-level evidence in a structured UI showing source comparison, validation results, recommended scope, and next action.

  • Source comparison across registry, network-collected, and customer asset files
  • Rule checks for end-of-support, coverage, ownership, address, SLA
  • AI explanation for conflict and review-required cases
  • Approve, reject, or request validation actions
Workflow 02

Prompt-based coverage policy generation

Asset Managers generate coverage policies using guided prompts. The system turns operational context into structured rules for sites, products, service levels, and exclusions.

  • Prompt-driven service coverage strategy
  • Critical site and critical product identification
  • Suggested SLA and entitlement rules
  • Human approval before rules apply
Workflow 03

Auto-import entitlements into coverage policies

Entitlement instructions and contract logic can be imported directly into coverage policies so the Asset Manager does not need to recreate them.

  • Extract entitlement instructions
  • Map to service coverage rules
  • Flag missing or conflicting instructions
  • Prepare rule set for Asset Manager review
Workflow 04

New asset discovery and auto-discovery recommendation

The system identifies newly discovered assets, checks whether they match scope, and proposes whether they should be added, excluded, or reviewed.

  • Detect new assets from network-collected and customer asset evidence
  • Compare against current baseline
  • Apply coverage policies and eligibility checks
  • Generate proposed add-to-contract or review action
09 · Agent responsibilities

Six agents. Each with one operational role. One orchestrator.

The agent model kept the AI focused. Instead of one model trying to do everything, each agent aligned to a specific enterprise workflow — and all of them passed through a single orchestrator that handles routing, retrieval, and approvals.

Agent ecosystem — orchestrator at the center, agents radiating out
Operational agent Orchestrator hub Routing edge
Onboarding Agent
Reads order data, identifies program type, resolves customer and engagement context.
Assignment Agent
Ranks candidate Asset Managers by region, workload, language, skill, then routes for Team Asset Manager approval.
Reconciliation Agent
Compares evidence, applies validation, recommends in-scope, out-of-scope, conflict, or review.
Coverage Policy Agent
Applies critical-site and critical-product rules; suggests new policies when patterns appear.
Discovery Agent
Finds new and moved assets, identifies auto-discovery candidates, proposes contract actions.
Narrative Agent
Creates onboarding summaries, reconciliation narratives, and customer-ready operational insights.
10 · Dynamic UI loading

The UI loaded based on the decision the agent produced.

Reusable UI components are populated dynamically from tool and agent responses. The experience behaves less like a static dashboard and more like a guided operational workspace.

Component

Component

Component

Component

Component

Principle

The system should surface the next decision, not make users search for it.

12 · Engineering challenges

The biggest effort was not adding AI. It was making enterprise operations AI-ready.

Three challenge clusters defined the work — implementation, RAG/agent governance, and data engineering. We've kept one or two of the most important challenges per cluster, with the engineering response on each.

Implementation challenges
Challenge

Fragmented source systems & identity

Different workflows depended on different systems for orders, contracts, customer identity, entitlement, coverage, and inventory evidence. The same customer or engagement could appear differently across them.

Response: A purpose-built operational data model with entity-resolution logic across order references, opportunity IDs, customer IDs, and account-hierarchy mapping.

Challenge

AI trust and explainability

Operational teams could not rely on recommendations without understanding why the system proposed them.

Response: Every AI-assisted recommendation carries source evidence, confidence, reasoning, and an approval workflow.

RAG & agent challenges
Challenge

Unstructured operational knowledge

Coverage rules, onboarding logic, and customer preferences lived in transcripts, spreadsheets, and tribal knowledge. Retrieval needed structure.

Response: A knowledge base indexed by workflow stage, persona, decision type, source system, and operational intent — with workflow-specific retrieval chains.

Challenge

Agents could not freely modify state

Coverage, contract, and onboarding actions affect real operational and financial workflows.

Response: A governed tool model. Agents interact only through approved APIs and rule services; every action returns evidence, confidence, and required permissions.

Data engineering challenges
Challenge

Warehouse data, application workflow

The data warehouse was strong for analytics, but application workflows needed fast, repeated reads and writes, and could not rely on traditional relational enforcement for engagement, order, and rule relationships.

Response: Purpose-built operational entities, semantic views, and controlled service-layer updates with validation before commit.

Challenge

Very large instance payloads

Bulk tagging, reconciliation, and asset operations could involve hundreds of thousands of instance IDs — far past practical query payload limits.

Response: Staged object-storage patterns and background flows so large payloads process safely without inline query bloat.

13 · Technology stack

How AI was wired into operational workflows — not bolted on.

The implementation combined enterprise data systems, backend APIs, workflow orchestration, object storage, RAG services, agent tooling, and dynamic UI components. AI is integrated through governed APIs, retrieval, evidence, and approvals — not exposed as an unrestricted chatbot.

Layer Technology How it was used
Frontend React · component-driven UI Role-based workbenches, AI review flows, evidence tables, recommendation drawers, coverage policy editors, approval queues.
Backend APIs Python · FastAPI · Pydantic Typed APIs for orders, engagements, allocation, reconciliation, coverage policies, and structured AI responses.
Data warehouse Enterprise data warehouse Primary store for orders, contracts, asset registry, entitlement, snapshots, and operational source joins.
Orchestration Prefect-style flows Long-running jobs for ingestion, refreshes, reconciliation, entitlement import, file processing, report generation.
Storage S3 · object storage Large network-collected and customer asset files, staged inputs, replayable evidence, async processing.
Data processing SQL · semantic views · staging tables Entity resolution, program classification, contract linkage, entitlement extraction, asset validation, snapshot comparison.
AI & RAG RAG + agent/tool architecture Retrieves operational context, calls approved tools, generates recommendations, returns UI-ready structured output.
Knowledge Indexed operational knowledge Process rules, purchase-program logic, coverage policies, lifecycle logic, validation rules.
Governance Role-based approvals · audit · confidence Keeps AI recommendations reviewable, explainable, and reversible before operational state changes.

Architectural principle. AI is integrated into enterprise workflows through governed APIs, tools, retrieval, evidence, and approvals — never exposed as an unrestricted chatbot over enterprise data.
